releases.name: opencodev2-cursor 0.1.9
releases.body:
# opencodev2-cursor 0.1.9

## What it changes

- Share one Cursor SDK worker across open projects and hosts.
- Keep quiet, live SDK runs open until the turn cap instead of failing at the idle timeout.
- Recover queued turns after tool continuations and host disconnects.
- Keep queued and late cancellations from stopping the active replacement request.
- Preserve non-ASCII prompts across socket chunks and clean up abort listeners.
- Share pending SDK connections and concurrent model-list requests.

## Limits

Verified on Windows 11 with one Cursor account. Linux, macOS, a second account and multi-minute quiet runs have not been live-tested. The latest disconnect, UTF-8 and cancellation fixes are covered by localhost integration tests with fake runners. This update does not make complex model generation faster.

## Upgrading

Run `opencode plugin update opencodev2-cursor`. Finish active chats, close every plugin host, including OpenChamber and OpenCode terminals, then reopen them. This lets the shared SDK worker load the new runtime. Public options and the OpenAI-compatible proxy request shape are unchanged.

## Tests

76 automated tests passed across 11 files. TypeScript build passed. Live Grok 4.7 read-tool calls and tool-result continuations passed through two local hosts, using JSON and SSE responses.

The attached `.tgz` is the npm package, not a platform-specific installer.

releases.name: opencodev2-cursor 0.1.7
releases.body:
# opencodev2-cursor 0.1.7

Historical release record for the version already published on npm. The annotated tag points to `7a5586b351b0e8d860b3d7e20b4c0b66f0a7c4f3`, the npm package's recorded gitHead. Its complete git tree matches the subsequently merged main commit `984be3d`.

## What it changes

- Use session-specific SDK locks so one chat's tool call does not block another chat.
- Recover late tool results on a fresh Cursor run instead of failing the chat.
- Increase the default idle timeout to 5 minutes, retaining the 15-minute overall turn cap.

## Limits

Originally verified on Windows with one Cursor account. Linux, macOS and a second account were not verified. This entry records the existing npm release; it does not republish the package.

## Upgrading

Prefer the latest npm release for the subsequent shared-worker fixes.

## Tests

The original handoff recorded 65 passing tests across 10 files and a passing build on 10/11/2026. These counts describe the historical version, not the current checkout.
